title: Annual source limits permit a fall in the Gulf river carbon-to-nitrate ratio despite a 9.65% point rise between 1996-2005 and 2016-2025
abstract: We tested dissolved organic carbon load per unit nitrate plus nitrite load at two Gulf river outlets with USGS release 3.0. Between 1996-2005 and 2016-2025, the combined ratio rose by 9.65% under stationary flow normalization. Carbon load fell by 3.57%, while nitrate load fell by 12.06%. The published marginal annual error limits permit ratio changes from -16.94% to +44.98%. This is a sensitivity bound, not a confidence interval. An adverse combination of errors one third of the way to those limits can erase the point rise. Generalized normalization and annual loads also gave positive point ratio changes, but annual loads showed increases in both constituents. The result does not resolve the true direction of ratio change or identify biological effects. Shared model error, retrospective fits, period choices and annual time resolution limit inference. Code, public CC0 inputs, provenance, all checks, an independent audit and a figure are included.

display.caption: Carbon-to-nitrate ratios, component load changes, and marginal source-limit sensitivity. Bounds are not confidence intervals.
